questions.question: Which language should the child and parent PWA use?
questions.rationale: A typed frontend supports the interactive learning flows and iPad-friendly PWA experience.

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Typed JavaScript for a maintainable PWA.

questions.question: Which framework should power the PWA?
questions.rationale: React is a practical default for a responsive, installable learning PWA.

options.label: React
options.description: A widely supported component framework with a mature PWA ecosystem.

options.label: Vue
options.description: A progressive framework for building interactive interfaces.

options.label: Angular
options.description: A full-featured framework with an integrated application structure.

questions.question: What should the PWA include in its first release?
questions.answer: Vietnamese child and parent interfaces; child profile and age-appropriate Math and Vietnamese activities; multiple-choice, answer-entry, and Vietnamese missing-letter questions; map-based question nodes; animated progress; iPad-friendly responsive layout; installable PWA shell.
questions.rationale: These features directly cover the learning, gameplay, language, and iPad requirements in Context.md.
questions.recommendedChoice: Vietnamese child and parent interfaces; child profile and age-appropriate Math and Vietnamese activities; multiple-choice, answer-entry, and Vietnamese missing-letter questions; map-based question nodes; animated progress; iPad-friendly responsive layout; installable PWA shell.

questions.question: Which language should the backend API use?
questions.rationale: TypeScript keeps the API contracts aligned with the PWA and supports a focused initial stack.

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Shared language and type-friendly contracts with the React frontend.

options.label: C# (.NET)
options.description: A strongly typed language on the .NET platform.

options.label: Python
options.description: A concise language with a broad web ecosystem.

questions.question: Which framework should serve the application API?
questions.rationale: Express keeps the first-version API straightforward while supporting question management, imports, and progress endpoints.

options.label: Express
options.description: A minimal, established Node.js web framework.

options.label: NestJS
options.description: A structured Node.js framework with TypeScript support.

questions.question: What should the backend support in its first release?
questions.answer: Parent authentication and administration; child profiles and age ranges; question bank CRUD for Math and Vietnamese; CSV question-and-answer import with age assignment and validation; answer checking and learning progress persistence.
questions.rationale: These are the smallest backend capabilities needed to make the requested child and parent workflows usable.
questions.recommendedChoice: Parent authentication and administration; child profiles and age ranges; question bank CRUD for Math and Vietnamese; CSV question-and-answer import with age assignment and validation; answer checking and learning progress persistence.

questions.question: Which persistent data stores are needed?
questions.rationale: Question sets and progress are relational; Blob Storage covers parent-uploaded import files.

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: Use only in-memory or client-side data; do not provision persistent storage.

options.label: PostgreSQL
options.description: Store parent accounts, child profiles, questions, and progress.

options.label: Azure Blob Storage
options.description: Store imported question-set files for processing and retention.

options.label: Azure SQL
options.description: Managed relational database for application records.

options.label: Azure Cosmos DB
options.description: Managed document database for flexible JSON data.

questions.question: Should parents sign in to manage children, questions, and imports?
questions.rationale: Parent-only administration requires protected access to child profiles and question management.

options.label: Yes
options.description: Parents sign in before using administration features.

options.label: No
options.description: Administration is available without application sign-in.
